privacy_intro: Morsewell is an independent Morse code trainer. You can practise as a guest, create an account to sync your progress, or take part in the public forum.
privacy_practice_body: As a guest, your answers, scores, lesson progress and preferences stay in this browser. If you sign in, Morsewell syncs account settings and training records across devices. You can choose to add practice that you saved as a guest to your account.
privacy_account_body: We store your username and email address to manage your account. If you use a password, we store its hash. Your browser stores Morsewell session tokens to keep you signed in. The site owner can view account details and training summaries when running the service and helping learners.
privacy_google_button: When Google sign-in is available, your browser connects to Google to display its button for sign-in, registration, account linking, or identity verification before you delete a Google-only account. Google sends Morsewell a signed ID token when you continue. We verify it and keep it only for that request.
privacy_google_identity: We store Google’s identifier for your account and the identity provider that issued it. At registration, we save your email address and use Google’s email verification and domain information to determine whether it needs further verification. Your Morsewell username is the one you choose. We do not store your Google profile photo or name, or request access to Gmail, Drive or your contacts.
privacy_forum_body: Anyone can read your forum posts and replies, including your username and the amateur radio callsign you choose to add to your profile. Other users cannot see your account email or synced training history.
privacy_contact_routing: Cloudflare forwards privacy and support emails to the same private Google Group managed by the Morsewell owner. Cloudflare and Google process your email address and message. You can also email the group directly.
privacy_providers_body: Our hosting services and Cloudflare process web requests, including IP addresses, to deliver and protect the site over HTTPS. Resend receives the recipient address and message content to deliver verification codes and any support or product emails you opt into. Morsewell has no advertising or third-party analytics.
privacy_local_controls: You can manage account details and email preferences in Settings. In Settings, signed-in users can export their data, reset learning progress, or permanently delete their account. Clearing the account history cache removes downloaded copies in this browser. Clearing all site data in your browser also erases guest practice and pending uploads on this device. Records already synced to your account remain on the server.
privacy_google_controls: If you remove Morsewell in your Google Account, Google will ask for your permission the next time you use Google sign-in. Morsewell keeps the Google identifier associated with your account, so Settings still shows Google as linked. You can delete your Morsewell account in Settings.
privacy_contact_body: Email the Morsewell owner privately to ask about your information or request deletion of your account or data. The owner will confirm that you control the account before acting on a deletion request.
privacy_retention_body: Morsewell keeps account and training records so you can return to them. Backup copies may remain until the backups rotate.

about_intro: Morsewell is a free Morse code trainer built around the Koch method — and this page is where the why, the who, and your data live.
about_koch_intro: The Koch method is a research-backed technique for learning Morse code, developed by German psychologist Ludwig Koch in the 1930s. Unlike traditional approaches that start slowly and speed up, Koch's method trains your brain to recognise characters at full speed from day one.
about_koch_step1_body: Begin by learning only two characters (K and M in the original method) played at your target speed — typically 20 WPM or faster.
about_koch_step2_body: Practice until you can copy those two characters with at least 90% accuracy. Accuracy is the gate, not time.
about_koch_step3_title: Add one character at a time
about_koch_step3_body: Once you hit the accuracy threshold, add one new character to your set and repeat the process. New characters are always introduced at full speed.
about_koch_step4_body: Gradually work through all 40+ Morse characters. Because every character was learned at speed, your brain develops instant recognition rather than counting dots and dashes.
about_koch_why_body: Learning at speed forces your brain to treat each character as a distinct sound pattern rather than a sequence of dots and dashes to decode. This is the same way fluent speakers process spoken language — whole words and sounds, not individual letters sounded out.
about_koch_vs_traditional_body: Start at 5 WPM, gradually increase speed. Result: speed plateaus are common and relearning at higher speeds is often required.
about_koch_vs_koch_body: Start at target speed (20+ WPM), expand character set. Result: learners reach operational speed faster with no speed plateau.
about_project_body: Morsewell is an independent project rather than a company. The frontend is SvelteKit and TypeScript, with Paraglide handling the five interface languages; the API is Gin and Go. The community forum is now live.
about_project_support: For general questions or help signing in, email Morsewell.
